devices.label: Server with agent
devices.summary: Linux, Windows, macOS or FreeBSD: CPU, memory, disks, network, Docker, services, backups.
devices.typical: Linux, Windows, Raspberry Pi, Hyper-V host

credentials.label: No authentication
credentials.help: Nothing is sent: the monitor answers without credentials.

setup.title: Install the agent on the machine
steps: In DumbMonit, save the monitor: an enrollment token (dmon_…) is shown once, with the install command ready to copy for Linux and for Windows.
Run that install command on the machine, with elevated rights (sudo on Linux and macOS, an elevated PowerShell on Windows).
The machine shows up within a few seconds, named after its host name.

Optional, for Docker: if the agent runs under a dedicated user, add that user to the "docker" group and restart the agent.
usermod -aG docker dumbmonit
For a fleet, or to revoke a lost token, use Settings → Agents.
setup.warning: The agent contacts the server, never the other way round: no port needs to be opened on the monitored machine.

rules.name: Monitor unreachable
rules.description: No measurement received for more than three minutes. bottomk by (target) (1, time() - tlast_over_time(dumbmonit_up[7d]))

rules.name: High CPU
rules.description: CPU load sustained above 90%, averaged per monitor across SNMP, Proxmox and agent sources; clears below 85 %.

rules.name: Unusual CPU
rules.description: CPU load noticeably different from the usual at this time and day of the week (seasonal baseline).

rules.name: Disk almost full
rules.description: Filesystem 90% full or more, per mount point (SNMP, Proxmox storages and root filesystems); clears below 88 %.

rules.name: Filesystem almost full
rules.description: At this rate, the filesystem will be full within four days.

rules.name: Disk SMART failing
rules.description: The disk's own SMART self-assessment reports it as failing. Replace it and check the backups.

rules.name: ZFS pool degraded
rules.description: A ZFS pool is no longer healthy: a device is missing, faulted or removed.

rules.name: ZFS scrub found errors
rules.description: The last ZFS scrub found errors on this pool, or files are permanently lost. The pool can stay ONLINE.

rules.name: Temperature above critical
rules.description: A sensor is above the critical temperature its own hardware declares; no fixed value.

rules.name: Container stopped
rules.description: The container has been stopped for two minutes. A container Docker would not restart is left out: a one-shot docker run that finished, a container never started, or one stopped by hand without a restart policy. A crash (any other exit code), an out-of-memory kill, or an always / unless-stopped container still counts.

rules.name: Container unhealthy
rules.description: The container's health check has been failing for three minutes. A stopped container is left out: Docker keeps its last verdict, which no longer means anything.

rules.name: Container restarting
rules.description: The container restarted three times or more in fifteen minutes (increase(dumbmonit_container_restart_count[15m])): it is rarely stopped long enough for the previous rule.

rules.name: Container update available
rules.description: A newer image is available in the registry for this container.

devices.label: Server hardware (Redfish)
devices.summary: Fans, temperatures, power supplies, drives and memory, read from the BMC (iDRAC, iLO…).
devices.typical: Server fans, temperatures, power supplies and drives, read from its BMC

setup.title: Create a read-only account on the management controller
steps: Open the web interface of the management controller (BMC), not the operating system of the server.

Create a local user named as follows, with a long password used nowhere else.
dumbmonit
Give it the read-only right of your vendor, listed below.
In DumbMonit, enter the controller address (bmc.lan or 10.0.0.50) with that user name and password.
setup.warning: Do not reuse the controller's factory account, which can power the server off and reflash the firmware; a self-signed certificate needs "Accept an unverifiable certificate" ticked.

rules.name: Server fan failed
rules.description: The management controller reports a fan as failed.

rules.name: Server temperature above critical
rules.description: A temperature sensor is above the critical threshold the controller itself declares.

rules.name: Power supply redundancy lost
rules.description: The power supplies are no longer redundant: one more failure and the server goes down.

rules.name: Power supply failed
rules.description: The controller reports a power supply as failed.

rules.name: Drive failure predicted
rules.description: A drive reports a predicted failure: replace it while it still works.

rules.name: Server health critical
rules.description: The controller reports the system's own health as Critical.

rules.name: Monitor unreachable
rules.description: No measurement received for more than three minutes. bottomk by (target) (1, time() - tlast_over_time(dumbmonit_up[7d]))

devices.label: UPS with NUT
devices.summary: UPS served by Network UPS Tools: on battery, low or worn-out battery, charge, runtime left, load and input voltage, for every UPS the server publishes.
examples: Synology or QNAP NAS with a USB UPS
devices.typical: UPS on a NAS, Raspberry Pi or server running Network UPS Tools

credentials.label: No authentication (recommended)
credentials.help: upsd lets any host it accepts read the UPS variables, without an account.

credentials.label: upsd user name / password
credentials.help: Sent with USERNAME and PASSWORD before reading. upsd does not check them to read; set them only if your setup asks for them.

setup.title: Let DumbMonit read the NUT server
steps:
On a plain NUT install, add this line to upsd.conf and restart upsd.
LISTEN 0.0.0.0 3493
Open TCP port 3493 in the firewall for the DumbMonit host.
On a NAS, enable its network UPS server instead: Synology DSM → Control Panel → Hardware & Power → UPS, then add the DumbMonit host under Permitted DiskStation Devices.

Optional, to name this client: add a user without actions or instcmds to upsd.users, with a long random password, and restart upsd.
[dumbmonit]
password = a-long-random-password
In DumbMonit, enter the NUT server's address (nas.lan): every UPS it publishes is watched.
setup.warning: DumbMonit watches the UPS; it shuts nothing down: the machines it powers still need their own NUT client (upsmon) to shut down cleanly.

rules.name: UPS on battery
rules.description: The UPS is powering the load from battery.

rules.name: UPS battery low
rules.description: The UPS battery is low or depleted.

rules.name: Monitor unreachable
rules.description: No measurement received for more than three minutes. bottomk by (target) (1, time() - tlast_over_time(dumbmonit_up[7d]))

devices.label: Active Directory
devices.summary: A Windows domain over LDAP, read-only: domain controllers and FSMO roles, privileged group members, password policy, and security findings such as Kerberos-roastable accounts, unconstrained delegation or an old krbtgt password.
devices.typical: Windows domain over LDAPS: domain controllers and FSMO roles, privileged group members, password policy, security findings

credentials.label: Service account
credentials.help: A plain domain user created for DumbMonit, member of no group.

setup.title: Create a read-only service account for DumbMonit
steps:
Active Directory Users and Computers → your domain → Users → New → User: name it as follows, set a long random password and add it to no group.
svc-dumbmonit
On its Account tab, tick Password never expires, or the bind fails the day the password does.

Optional, to see inbound replication status: grant the account the right listed below on the domain object.
dsacls "DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com" /G "CORP\svc-dumbmonit:CA;Monitor active directory replication"
For LDAPS, export your certification authority's certificate as Base-64 encoded X.509 and paste it as CA certificate below.
In DumbMonit, enter a domain controller's name as its certificate names it (dc1.corp.example.com) and log in as svc-dumbmonit@corp.example.com.
setup.warning: Plain LDAP on port 389 sends the password in clear and is refused by default: use LDAPS, or StartTLS on port 389.

rules.name: Domain controller unreachable
rules.description: A domain controller of the domain no longer answers on its LDAP port. A name that does not resolve from DumbMonit produces no series and never fires.

rules.name: Active Directory bind failed
rules.description: The domain controller answers but refuses the service account: expired password, disabled or locked-out account.

rules.name: Privileged group membership changed
rules.description: A member joined or left Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Schema Admins, Administrators or an operators group, nesting included (changes_prometheus(dumbmonit_ad_privileged_group_fingerprint[1h]), label group). Resolves by itself an hour later.

rules.name: Active Directory replication failing
rules.description: The queried domain controller cannot replicate from a partner. Only when the account may read replication status.

rules.name: krbtgt password older than 180 days
rules.description: The krbtgt password was last changed more than 180 days ago.

rules.name: Monitor unreachable
rules.description: No measurement received for more than three minutes. bottomk by (target) (1, time() - tlast_over_time(dumbmonit_up[7d]))

devices.label: SNMP device
devices.summary: Switches, routers, UPS, printers, access points: anything that answers SNMP.
devices.typical: Switch, router, NAS, UPS, printer

credentials.label: SNMP v1 / v2c (community)
credentials.help: The simplest form: one shared word, sent unencrypted.

credentials.label: SNMP v3 (user, authentication, privacy)
credentials.help: Authenticated and encrypted. Needs a USM user on the device.

setup.title: Enable SNMP on the device
steps: Open the device's web interface and find its SNMP settings, often under Network, Services or Administration.
Enable SNMP v2c and note the read-only community (public on many devices).
If the device filters by address, allow this server's address.
In DumbMonit, enter the address and the community: the rest is detected automatically.
setup.warning: A community is not encrypted on the network: on a shared network, prefer SNMP v3, which authenticates and encrypts.

rules.name: High CPU
rules.description: CPU load sustained above 90%, averaged per monitor across SNMP, Proxmox and agent sources; clears below 85 %.

rules.name: Unusual CPU
rules.description: CPU load noticeably different from the usual at this time and day of the week (seasonal baseline).

rules.name: Disk almost full
rules.description: Filesystem 90% full or more, per mount point (SNMP, Proxmox storages and root filesystems); clears below 88 %.

rules.name: Filesystem almost full
rules.description: At this rate, the filesystem will be full within four days.

rules.name: UPS on battery
rules.description: The UPS is powering the load from battery.

rules.name: UPS battery low
rules.description: The UPS battery is low or depleted.

rules.name: Port accumulating errors
rules.description: A network port logged more than fifty errors in the last hour: usually a failing cable, a dirty fibre or a duplex mismatch (increase_prometheus(dumbmonit_if_errors_in[1h]) + increase_prometheus(dumbmonit_if_errors_out[1h]); nothing fires during the first hour of a new monitor, so errors counted before it was added are not reported as new).

rules.name: Port flapping
rules.description: A network port went down and up again more than twice in thirty minutes (changes_prometheus(dumbmonit_if_oper_status[30m])). A port disabled on purpose has no series and never fires.

rules.name: Monitor unreachable
rules.description: No measurement received for more than three minutes. bottomk by (target) (1, time() - tlast_over_time(dumbmonit_up[7d]))

devices.label: MikroTik RouterOS
devices.summary: RouterOS and RouterBOOT versions behind, CPU, memory, temperatures, fans and power supplies, and errors and link losses on every interface.
devices.typical: Router or switch: versions and firmware behind, CPU, memory, sensors, interface errors

credentials.label: Read-only user
credentials.help: The dumbmonit user created above, in the dumbmonit-read group. Sent as HTTP basic authentication.

setup.title: Create a read-only user on the router
steps:
WinBox or WebFig → System → Users → Groups → Add: name the group as follows and tick only the policies listed below.
dumbmonit-read

System → Users → Add: create the user dumbmonit in that group, with a long random password.
dumbmonit
IP → Services: enable www-ssl and pick a certificate (create one under System → Certificates).

Optional, to hear about new RouterOS versions: System → Scheduler → Add, interval 1d, start time startup, with this On Event script.
/system package update check-for-updates once
In DumbMonit, enter the router's address (192.168.88.1) with that user name and password.
setup.warning: RouterOS 7.1 or later is required (RouterOS 6 has no REST API); with a self-signed certificate, tick "Accept an unverifiable certificate" in the options.

rules.name: MikroTik CPU high
rules.description: The router's CPU has stayed above 90 %: routing, the firewall or a script is saturating it. Clears below 80 %.

rules.name: Monitor unreachable
rules.description: No measurement received for more than three minutes. bottomk by (target) (1, time() - tlast_over_time(dumbmonit_up[7d]))

devices.label: UniFi Network
devices.summary: The UniFi network and what it manages: gateways, switches and access points offline or waiting for adoption, firmware updates, WAN and Internet status, clients and alarms, and the last connection of the clients you mark as worth watching.
examples: UniFi OS console (Dream Machine, Cloud Gateway, Cloud Key)
devices.typical: UniFi console or self-hosted server: devices, WAN, clients

credentials.label: API key (UniFi OS console)
credentials.help: Reads devices, their load and the client count through the official Integration API. Created in Settings → Control Plane → Integrations.

credentials.label: View Only account
credentials.help: A local account with the View Only role. Also reads the WAN, Internet and alarm status, and works on a self-hosted server.

setup.title: Create a read-only access in UniFi Network
steps: For an API key on a UniFi OS console: UniFi Network → Settings → Control Plane → Integrations → Create API Key. Name it DumbMonit and copy it: it is shown once.

Or create a local account (needed for WAN and alarm status, and on a self-hosted server): Settings → Admins & Users → Create New, local access only.
dumbmonit
Set that account's UniFi Network role to View Only.
In DumbMonit, enter the address (unifi.lan, or unifi.lan:8443 for a self-hosted server) and paste the key or the account.
If the network is not the default site, set the Site option to the short name shown after /manage/ or /network/ in the address bar.
setup.warning: Use a local account, never the owner or a UI.com cloud account, and accept the console's self-signed certificate in the options unless you installed your own.

rules.name: UniFi device offline
rules.description: A UniFi device adopted by the controller is offline, isolated or failed to adopt.

rules.name: UniFi Internet down
rules.description: The UniFi gateway reports no Internet connection. Without a UniFi gateway the series does not exist and the rule stays silent.

rules.name: UniFi WAN link down
rules.description: A WAN link of the UniFi gateway is down: with two links, redundancy is lost while nothing seems broken. A disabled port has no series.

rules.name: UniFi gateway CPU high
rules.description: The UniFi gateway's processor has been above 90% for fifteen minutes; clears below 80 %.

rules.name: UniFi device waiting for adoption
rules.description: A device appeared on the network and waits to be adopted in UniFi.

rules.name: UniFi firmware update available
rules.description: A firmware update is available for UniFi devices.

rules.name: UniFi alarms
rules.description: UniFi logged critical events or raised alarms in the last 24 hours. Only read with a View Only account.

rules.name: Monitor unreachable
rules.description: No measurement received for more than three minutes. bottomk by (target) (1, time() - tlast_over_time(dumbmonit_up[7d]))

devices.label: Tailscale
devices.summary: The devices of a tailnet through the Tailscale API: servers offline, node keys about to expire, devices awaiting approval, clients to update, and each device's last connection.
devices.typical: Tailnet: servers offline, node keys expiring, devices awaiting approval
devices.credential: OAuth client (devices:core:read) or API access token

credentials.label: OAuth client
credentials.help: Recommended: a client limited to the devices:core:read scope, which can change nothing.

credentials.label: API access token
credentials.help: Works too, but carries every right of the user who created it and expires after 90 days at most.

setup.title: Create a read-only OAuth client for DumbMonit
steps: In the Tailscale console (login.tailscale.com), open Settings → Trust credentials → Credential → OAuth.
Tick only the read scope listed below, then click Generate credential.
Copy the client ID and the client secret (tskey-client-...): the secret is shown once.
In DumbMonit, enter api.tailscale.com as address and paste them as Client ID and Client secret; leave the Tailnet option empty.
setup.warning: Only tagged devices (servers, subnet routers, exit nodes) are expected to stay online: name the ones to watch in the Devices to keep online option, or enter all.

rules.name: Tailscale device offline
rules.description: A Tailscale device that must stay online (a tagged device by default) has been disconnected for more than 15 minutes (dumbmonit_tailscale_device_offline_seconds and on (target, device) dumbmonit_tailscale_device_watched > 0).

rules.name: Tailscale node key expiring
rules.description: A Tailscale device's node key expires in less than 14 days: it will leave the tailnet until someone signs it in again.

rules.name: Tailscale device awaiting approval
rules.description: A device joined the tailnet and awaits approval: approve it if it is expected, remove it otherwise.

rules.name: Tailscale client update
rules.description: A Tailscale device that must stay online runs a client with an update available (dumbmonit_tailscale_device_update_available and on (target, device) dumbmonit_tailscale_device_watched > 0).

rules.name: Monitor unreachable
rules.description: No measurement received for more than three minutes. bottomk by (target) (1, time() - tlast_over_time(dumbmonit_up[7d]))

devices.label: OpenVPN server
devices.summary: An OpenVPN server through its management interface: version, whether it reports itself connected, and every client currently in session with its addresses and traffic.
devices.typical: OpenVPN server through its management interface: version, state, connected clients

credentials.label: No password
credentials.help: Only for a management interface started without a password-file argument.

credentials.label: Management password
credentials.help: The shared password set by the third argument of the server's "management" directive.

setup.title: Turn on the management interface
steps:
Add this line to the server's configuration (server.conf, or as.conf on OpenVPN Access Server) and restart OpenVPN.
management 0.0.0.0 7505

Recommended: protect it with a password, put in a file readable by the OpenVPN process alone and added as a third argument.
management 0.0.0.0 7505 /etc/openvpn/management-password
In DumbMonit, enter the server's address (vpn.lan, port 7505) and the management password if one is set.
setup.warning: Anyone who reaches the management port and knows the password can disconnect clients and reconfigure the running server: allow only the DumbMonit host in the firewall and set a password.

rules.name: Monitor unreachable
rules.description: No measurement received for more than three minutes. bottomk by (target) (1, time() - tlast_over_time(dumbmonit_up[7d]))

devices.label: OPNsense
devices.summary: Gateway latency and loss, VPN tunnels, DHCP leases, services and pending updates.
devices.typical: Firewall, router, multi-WAN edge

credentials.label: API key and secret
credentials.help: The two lines of the file OPNsense downloads when the key is created.

setup.title: Create a read-only API key in OPNsense
steps:
System → Access → Groups → Add: name the group as follows.
dumbmonit
In that group, under Assigned Privileges, add the privileges listed below.

System → Access → Users → Add: name the user as follows, generate a password, and make it a member of that group.
dumbmonit
Edit the user, click + under API keys, and save the downloaded file: it holds the key and the secret, shown only once.
In DumbMonit, enter the firewall address (192.168.1.1 or fw.lan:8443), the key as API key and the secret as API secret.
setup.warning: An API key is a password that never expires: restrict the group's source networks to the DumbMonit host and never grant All pages. OPNsense ships a self-signed certificate: tick "Accept an unverifiable certificate" if the connection is refused.

rules.name: Internet gateway down
rules.description: dpinger no longer gets an answer from a gateway. On a multi-WAN firewall the traffic has already moved to another link, quietly. loss and delay are warnings, not failures, and do not fire this rule.

rules.name: Gateway losing packets
rules.description: A gateway is losing more than a fifth of the packets sent to it: the link answers, badly. Clears below 10 %.

rules.name: Gateway slow
rules.description: A gateway's round-trip time has stayed above 300 ms. Three hundred milliseconds leaves a mobile backup link alone.

rules.name: Firewall state table filling up
rules.description: pf is tracking more than 80 % of the connections it is allowed. Past the limit the firewall drops new connections with no other symptom.

rules.name: Firewall network buffers exhausted
rules.description: More than 90 % of the FreeBSD network buffers are in use. A firewall that runs out stops forwarding with the CPU still idle.

rules.name: VPN tunnel down
rules.description: A configured VPN tunnel has had no session for ten minutes. A plugin that is not installed, or a connection that is disabled, has no series and cannot fire.

rules.name: Firewall resolver stopped
rules.description: Unbound has stopped answering. The firewall still routes; the machines behind it no longer resolve. Turn this rule off if your firewall resolves with something else.

rules.name: Firewall core service stopped
rules.description: dpinger, which watches the gateways, or configd, which runs everything else, is stopped. Only those two, because a service switched off on purpose is not a failure.

rules.name: Firewall too hot
rules.description: A sensor reads above 85 °C: the fanless box in the cupboard is about to start throttling. Clears at 78 °C.

rules.name: Firewall left in CARP maintenance mode
rules.description: CARP has been left in persistent maintenance mode: this firewall handed its virtual addresses to its partner and will not take them back on its own.

rules.name: Firewall reboot pending
rules.description: An update is installed but needs a reboot to take effect.

rules.name: Firewall updates pending
rules.description: The firewall has packages waiting to be updated. It is the most exposed machine on the network.

devices.label: pfSense
devices.summary: A pfSense firewall through its REST API package: gateways down or losing packets, interfaces without link, stopped services, CPU, memory and disk.
devices.typical: Firewall: gateways down or lossy, interfaces without link, stopped services

credentials.label: REST API key
credentials.help: The key created for the dumbmonit user: it carries only that user's read privileges.

setup.title: Create a read-only REST API key for DumbMonit
steps:
Install the pfSense-pkg-RESTAPI package (version 2) from Diagnostics → Command Prompt, with the file matching your pfSense version (2.7.2 below).
pkg-static add https://github.com/pfrest/pfSense-pkg-RESTAPI/releases/latest/download/pfSense-2.7.2-pkg-RESTAPI.pkg
System → REST API → Settings: tick both BasicAuth and Key among the authentication methods.
System → User Manager → Users → Add: create the user dumbmonit with a long random password.
Edit the user and, under Assigned Privileges, add the privileges listed below.

Create the key as dumbmonit, copy the key value of the answer, then remove the POST privilege again.
curl -k -u dumbmonit -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"descr":"DumbMonit"}' https://pfsense.lan/api/v2/auth/key
In DumbMonit, enter the pfSense address (pfsense.lan) and paste the key as API key.
setup.warning: The REST API package is a community project, not part of pfSense: reinstall it after each pfSense upgrade. pfSense ships a self-signed certificate: tick "Accept an unverifiable certificate" unless you replaced it.

rules.name: pfSense gateway down
rules.description: A pfSense gateway is down: its monitor address no longer answers, and the traffic it carries stops or fails over.

rules.name: pfSense gateway losing packets
rules.description: A pfSense gateway loses more than 10 % of the probes to its monitor address: the line is degraded (dumbmonit_pfsense_gateway_loss_percent unless on (target, gateway) dumbmonit_pfsense_gateway_up == 0).

rules.name: pfSense gateway slow
rules.description: The round trip to a pfSense gateway's monitor address has stayed above 500 ms for fifteen minutes.

rules.name: pfSense interface without link
rules.description: An enabled pfSense interface has no link: cable, switch port or network card.

rules.name: pfSense service stopped
rules.description: A pfSense service that is enabled is not running: DNS resolver, VPN, NTP….

rules.name: pfSense disk nearly full
rules.description: The pfSense disk is more than 90 % full: logs, reports and package updates stop being written.

rules.name: Monitor unreachable
rules.description: No measurement received for more than three minutes. bottomk by (target) (1, time() - tlast_over_time(dumbmonit_up[7d]))

devices.label: FortiGate
devices.summary: A Fortinet firewall through the FortiOS REST API: IPsec tunnels down, interfaces without link, HA out of sync, memory near conserve mode, FortiGuard licences expiring.
devices.typical: Firewall: IPsec tunnels, links, HA sync, conserve mode, FortiGuard licences
devices.credential: REST API token (read-only profile, trusted host)

credentials.label: API token
credentials.help: The token of the dumbmonit REST API user, sent as a bearer token.

setup.title: Create a read-only REST API user for DumbMonit
steps:
System → Admin Profiles → Create New: name the profile as follows and set the access permissions listed below, everything else None.
dumbmonit-ro

System → Administrators → Create New → REST API Admin: name it as follows and pick that profile.
dumbmonit
Under Trusted Hosts, enter the DumbMonit server's address with a /32 mask: FortiGate refuses 0.0.0.0/0.
Click OK: FortiGate shows the API token once. Copy it.
In DumbMonit, enter the FortiGate address (fw.lan) and paste the token as API token.
setup.warning: FortiGate ships a self-signed certificate: tick "Accept an unverifiable certificate" unless you installed your own.

rules.name: FortiGate IPsec tunnel down
rules.description: No phase 2 of a FortiGate site-to-site IPsec tunnel is up: the site behind it is cut off.

rules.name: FortiGate interface without link
rules.description: An enabled FortiGate interface with an address has no link: cable, transceiver or the device in front.

rules.name: FortiGate HA out of sync
rules.description: The members of a FortiGate HA cluster no longer have the same configuration checksum: a failover would run another configuration.

rules.name: FortiGate HA member lost
rules.description: A FortiGate HA cluster has fewer members than in the last 24 hours: there is no standby any more (max_over_time(dumbmonit_fortigate_ha_members[1d]) - dumbmonit_fortigate_ha_members).

rules.name: FortiGate memory near conserve mode
rules.description: FortiGate memory has stayed above 85 % for ten minutes: at 88 % (by default) it enters conserve mode and stops inspecting new sessions.

rules.name: FortiGate CPU high
rules.description: FortiGate CPU has stayed above 90 % for fifteen minutes.

rules.name: FortiGate licence expiring
rules.description: A FortiGuard or FortiCare licence of the FortiGate expires in less than 30 days, or has expired.

rules.name: FortiGate firmware update
rules.description: FortiGuard offers a newer patch release of the FortiOS branch the FortiGate runs.

rules.name: Monitor unreachable
rules.description: No measurement received for more than three minutes. bottomk by (target) (1, time() - tlast_over_time(dumbmonit_up[7d]))

devices.label: Sophos Firewall
devices.summary: A Sophos Firewall (SFOS) through its XML API: the link of every interface in a zone, and which IPsec connections are activated. Its live tunnel, HA and licence state are not in that API.
devices.typical: Firewall: interface links only (the XML API exposes no tunnel, HA or licence state)

credentials.label: User name and password
credentials.help: The dumbmonit user, whose device access profile is read-only everywhere.

setup.title: Allow DumbMonit to read the Sophos Firewall XML API
steps: Profiles → Device access: add a profile named DumbMonit read-only and set every permission to Read-only.

Authentication → Users: add a user named dumbmonit, of type Administrator, with that profile and a long random password.
dumbmonit
Backup & firmware → API (Administration → API access from SFOS 22): turn on the API configuration and add the DumbMonit server's address to the allowed IP addresses.
In DumbMonit, enter the firewall address (sophos.lan) with that user name and password.
setup.warning: The API listens on the administration port (4444 by default) with a self-signed certificate: tick "Accept an unverifiable certificate" unless you installed your own.

rules.name: Sophos interface without link
rules.description: A Sophos Firewall interface that is switched on and bound to a zone has no link.

rules.name: Monitor unreachable
rules.description: No measurement received for more than three minutes. bottomk by (target) (1, time() - tlast_over_time(dumbmonit_up[7d]))

devices.label: Proxmox VE
devices.summary: Nodes, virtual machines, containers, storage and backups of a Proxmox server or cluster.

setup.title: Create a read-only user and token in Proxmox VE
steps:
Open Datacenter → Permissions → Users → Add, enter the user name dumbmonit, choose the realm Proxmox VE authentication server, then click Add.
dumbmonit@pve
Open Datacenter → Permissions → Add → User Permission: path /, user dumbmonit@pve, role PVEAuditor, then click Add.

Open Datacenter → Permissions → API Tokens → Add: user dumbmonit@pve, Token ID monitor, untick Privilege Separation, then click Add.
dumbmonit@pve!monitor

setup.title: Give DumbMonit a read-only XAPI account
steps:
On every host of the pool, create a local account with a long random password.
useradd -M -s /sbin/nologin dumbmonit
passwd dumbmonit

On the pool coordinator, turn on PAM authentication once.
xe pool-enable-external-auth auth-type=PAM service-name=pam

Register the account as a subject and note the UUID it prints.
xe subject-add subject-name=dumbmonit

Give that subject the built-in read-only role, with the UUID.
xe subject-role-add uuid=SUBJECT_UUID role-name=read-only
In DumbMonit, enter the address of the pool coordinator (for example xcp01.lan) with that user name and password.
setup.warning: If the pool already uses Active Directory, create the account there and skip steps 1 and 2. XCP-ng uses a self-signed certificate: enable "Accept an unverifiable certificate" unless the DumbMonit host trusts it.

credentials.label: Service account token
credentials.help: The token of the dumbmonit service account, read from its dumbmonit-token Secret.

setup.title: Create a read-only service account for DumbMonit
steps:
Create the service account.
kubectl create serviceaccount dumbmonit -n kube-system

Create a ClusterRole that can only get and list what DumbMonit reads.
kubectl create clusterrole dumbmonit-read --verb=get,list --resource=nodes,pods,persistentvolumeclaims,events,deployments.apps,statefulsets.apps,daemonsets.apps

Bind the role to the service account.
kubectl create clusterrolebinding dumbmonit-read --clusterrole=dumbmonit-read --serviceaccount=kube-system:dumbmonit

Create a token that does not expire, then print the token and the cluster CA in base64.
echo '{"apiVersion":"v1","kind":"Secret","metadata":{"name":"dumbmonit-token","namespace":"kube-system","annotations":{"kubernetes.io/service-account.name":"dumbmonit"}},"type":"kubernetes.io/service-account-token"}' | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n kube-system get secret dumbmonit-token -o jsonpath='{.data.token}' | base64 -d
kubectl -n kube-system get secret dumbmonit-token -o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}'
In DumbMonit, enter the API server address (for example https://k3s.lan:6443), paste the token as Service account token and the CA as Cluster CA certificate.
setup.warning: On k3s, run each command as sudo k3s kubectl. The API server certificate only lists its own names and addresses: use one it lists, or tick Accept an unverifiable certificate.

setup.title: Create a monitoring account in DSM
steps:
In DSM, open Control Panel → User & Group → User → Create and name the account as follows, with a long password used nowhere else.
dumbmonit
Join groups: tick administrators.
Assign shared folder permissions: tick No access on every shared folder.
Assign application permissions: Deny every application except DSM, and Active Backup for Business if you want its tasks read.
Keep two-step verification off for this account (Control Panel → Security → Account).
In DumbMonit, enter the NAS address (HTTPS, port 5001 by default) and this account's user name and password.
setup.warning: The administrators group is required by DSM's storage API, not by DumbMonit: that is why the account gets no shared folder and no other application.

setup.title: Create an API key for DumbMonit in TrueNAS
steps:
Open Credentials → Groups → Add, name the group as follows and give it the Local Administrator privilege.
dumbmonit

Open Credentials → Users → Add, name the account as follows and make dumbmonit its primary group. Leave shell access, sudo and SSH off.
dumbmonit
Open Credentials → Users → API Keys → Add, pick the dumbmonit user, name the key and copy it: TrueNAS shows it only once.

setup.title: Create a read-only user and token in Proxmox Backup Server

setup.title: Create a dedicated user and a long-lived token in Home Assistant
steps:
Open Settings → People → Users → Add user (turn on Advanced mode in your profile if the tab is missing), name the user as follows and give it a long random password.
dumbmonit
Log in as that user, open its profile (bottom of the sidebar) → Security → Long-lived access tokens → Create token, name it and copy it: it is shown only once.
In DumbMonit, enter the Home Assistant address (for example homeassistant.local, port 8123) and paste the token.

credentials.label: App password (recommended)
credentials.help: Generated under Settings → Web interface / API in expert mode. It cannot change Pi-hole's settings.

credentials.label: No password
credentials.help: Only for a Pi-hole whose web interface has no password at all.

setup.title: Create an app password in Pi-hole
steps: In Pi-hole's web interface, open Settings → Web interface / API and switch the page from Basic to Expert.
Click Configure app password, copy the password shown, then click Enable new app password.
Check that Settings → All settings → Webserver and API → webserver.api.app_sudo is off, its default.
In DumbMonit, enter Pi-hole's address and paste the app password, or pick No password if the web interface has none.
setup.warning: Pi-hole v6 or later is required; the app password can still pause blocking and edit lists through the API, so keep it for DumbMonit only.

rules.name: Pi-hole blocking disabled
rules.description: Blocking is off, paused or failed. The hold lets a five-minute pause from the web interface go by.

rules.description: The blocklists (gravity) have not been rebuilt for more than eight days: the weekly update fails.

rules.description: A newer version is available: the image in Docker, core, web interface or FTL otherwise. Pi-hole checks once a day.

devices.typical: DNS filter: protection, blocks, filter lists, upstream servers, updates

credentials.label: User name / password
credentials.help: The dedicated user added to AdGuardHome.yaml, sent as HTTP basic authentication.

credentials.label: No authentication
credentials.help: Only for an AdGuard Home with no user at all in AdGuardHome.yaml.

setup.title: Add a user for DumbMonit to AdGuard Home
steps:
Make a bcrypt hash of a long random password (htpasswd comes with apache2-utils or httpd-tools).
htpasswd -B -C 10 -n -b dumbmonit 'LONG-RANDOM-PASSWORD'

Stop AdGuard Home, add this line under users: in AdGuardHome.yaml with HASH replaced by the printed hash, then start it again.
- { name: dumbmonit, password: "HASH" }
In DumbMonit, enter the address of the AdGuard Home web interface, then the user dumbmonit and its password.
setup.warning: AdGuard Home has no read-only user, so dumbmonit can change every setting: keep its password to DumbMonit alone, and turn on HTTPS in Settings → Encryption settings across an untrusted network.

rules.name: AdGuard Home protection off
rules.description: Protection disabled, or paused and not back yet.

devices.typical: Security engine: decisions, alerts, bouncers that stopped pulling, log reading

credentials.label: Metrics only
credentials.help: Reads /metrics, and /health of the Local API. Nothing to create.

credentials.label: Bouncer API key
credentials.help: Also proves the Local API answers decision queries. A bouncer key can only read decisions.

setup.title: Let DumbMonit read CrowdSec's metrics
steps:
Make the metrics reachable: set listen_addr in the prometheus section of /etc/crowdsec/config.yaml to an address DumbMonit can reach, then restart CrowdSec.
sudo sed -i 's/listen_addr: 127.0.0.1/listen_addr: 0.0.0.0/' /etc/crowdsec/config.yaml
sudo systemctl restart crowdsec

Check from the DumbMonit host that the metrics answer on port 6060, and filter that port so only the DumbMonit host reaches it.
curl -s http://crowdsec.lan:6060/metrics | grep cs_info
DumbMonit also checks the Local API on port 8080 of the same host: untick Check the Local API for a host that only runs an agent.

Optional: create a bouncer key and paste it as Bouncer API key below.
sudo cscli bouncers add dumbmonit
In DumbMonit, enter the CrowdSec host, for example "crowdsec.lan".
setup.warning: A bouncer that stops pulling keeps enforcing a frozen list: DumbMonit warns when a bouncer's requests stop for 30 minutes.

rules.name: CrowdSec Local API down
rules.description: The Local API does not answer /health.

rules.name: CrowdSec bouncer stopped pulling
rules.description: A bouncer's requests did not change in 30 minutes (changes_prometheus(dumbmonit_crowdsec_bouncer_requests_total[30m])).

rules.name: CrowdSec reads no logs
rules.description: Not a single log line read in six hours (increase_prometheus(dumbmonit_crowdsec_lines_read_total[6h])).

rules.name: Monitor unreachable
rules.description: No measurement received for more than three minutes. bottomk by (target) (1, time() - tlast_over_time(dumbmonit_up[7d]))

setup.title: Monitor a mail relay
steps: In DumbMonit, enter the mail server, for example smtp.example.com:2525 (the usual port for the encryption by default).
Pick the encryption: STARTTLS for port 587, TLS for port 465, None for a relay on your own network on port 25.
Optional: fill in an account, to check that the relay still accepts it (a refused password is not reported as an outage).
Optional: name an Expected extension, such as STARTTLS, to be warned when the relay stops advertising it.

devices.label: MDaemon Email Server
devices.summary: Needs the agent on the Windows server: mail queues, sessions, Windows services and disk space, plus the mail ports answering and, optionally, the XML API.
devices.typical: Mail server: agent-read queues, sessions and Windows services, plus SMTP, IMAP, POP3, webmail, version
devices.credential: none (agent on the server required), or email address/password

credentials.label: Services only
credentials.help: Nothing is sent: DumbMonit connects to the mail ports and reads their greetings.

credentials.label: XML API account (optional, version only)
credentials.help: Also reads the version through the XML API. Leave the credential empty to watch the mail services only.

setup.title: Install the agent on the MDaemon server, then add this monitor
steps: On the Windows server that runs MDaemon, add a Server with agent monitor in DumbMonit and run its PowerShell command in an elevated PowerShell. The agent finds MDaemon by itself.
Back here, enter the server address and choose that agent in Agent installed on this server. DumbMonit pre-selects the one with the same host name.
Leave the credential on Services only: the agent already brings the queues, sessions, Windows services and disk space, and the mail ports are checked from DumbMonit.

Optional, only to read the exact version: open Accounts → Account Manager → New account and create the account below, with a long unique password.
dumbmonit@example.com
Allow the address DumbMonit connects from in Setup → XML API Service → Address Restrictions (Setup → XML API Management on MDaemon 26), then enter the account's full email address and its password.

To check more ports than SMTP, IMAP and webmail, set the Services option to a list like this one.
smtp,msa,imap,pop3,imaps,webmail
setup.warning: The queues, sessions and Windows services of MDaemon can only be read on the server itself: without the agent, DumbMonit sees the mail ports and nothing else. The XML API account is optional and only brings the version; MDaemon has no read-only role for it, so never reuse your own account, and use a password found nowhere else, as repeated failures can get DumbMonit blocked.

rules.name: MDaemon mail service down
rules.description: A watched mail service of the MDaemon server does not answer, or greets to refuse service. Only the services listed on the monitor have a series. The notification names the service and its port.

rules.name: MDaemon XML API not answering
rules.description: The XML API has stopped answering while the mail services still do: Remote Administration is probably stopped. Only a monitor with an account has the series.

rules.name: MDaemon mail queue growing
rules.description: The inbound, local or remote queue has grown by more than a hundred messages in two hours (delta(dumbmonit_mdaemon_queue_messages{queue=~"inbound\|local\|remote"}[2h])): MDaemon has stopped delivering from it. Read by the [agent](../devices/agent.md#windows-performance-counters) on the MDaemon server, so the alert is on the agent's monitor.

rules.name: MDaemon Bad queue not empty
rules.description: Messages are waiting in the Bad queue: MDaemon could neither deliver nor bounce them, and they stay there until an administrator releases or deletes them.

rules.name: MDaemon Retry queue high
rules.description: More than fifty messages wait in the Retry queue: remote servers keep refusing mail temporarily.

rules.name: Mail server Windows service stopped
rules.description: A Windows service of MDaemon or SecurityGateway that starts automatically is not running. Read by the [agent](../devices/agent.md) on the mail server, so the alert is on the agent's monitor. Services set to manual start or disabled do not alert.

rules.name: Mail queue stuck
rules.description: The oldest message of an inbound, local or remote queue has been waiting for more than two hours: the queue is frozen or delivery is blocked. Counted from the queue folders by the agent on the mail server.

rules.name: MDaemon queue frozen
rules.description: MDaemon reports one of its queues as frozen: it no longer processes it. Read from the performance counters by the agent on the mail server.

rules.name: Monitor unreachable
rules.description: No measurement received for more than three minutes. bottomk by (target) (1, time() - tlast_over_time(dumbmonit_up[7d]))

devices.label: SecurityGateway for Email Servers
devices.summary: Needs the agent on the Windows server: Windows services, mail queue folders and disk space, plus the gateway ports answering and the REST API counters (12.5 and later).
devices.typical: Mail gateway: agent-read Windows services and queues, delivery queue and other counters
devices.credential: none (agent on the server required), or API key

credentials.label: Services only
credentials.help: Nothing is sent: DumbMonit connects to the mail ports and reads their greetings.

credentials.label: API key (12.5 and later, recommended)
credentials.help: Also reads the version and the performance counters through the REST API. Leave the credential empty to watch the services only.

setup.title: Install the agent on the gateway server, then add this monitor
steps: On the Windows server that runs SecurityGateway, add a Server with agent monitor in DumbMonit and run its PowerShell command in an elevated PowerShell. The agent finds SecurityGateway by itself.
Back here, enter the gateway address and choose that agent in Agent installed on this server. DumbMonit pre-selects the one with the same host name.

Recommended, for the performance counters: in SecurityGateway 12.5 or later, open Setup/Users → Accounts → Administrators → New and create the account below, with a long unique password.
dumbmonit
Give the account the role listed below, and restrict it to the DumbMonit address in IP Restriction Options.
Sign in as that account, open Setup/Users → Accounts → API Keys and create a key with an expiry date, then paste the key in DumbMonit.

To check more ports than SMTP and the web interface, set the Services option to a list like this one.
smtp,web_https

SecurityGateway has no read-only role or narrower key: create the key from the dedicated account, never your own, and give it an expiry date.

rules.name: Mail server Windows service stopped
rules.description: A Windows service of MDaemon or SecurityGateway that starts automatically is not running. Read by the [agent](../devices/agent.md) on the mail server, so the alert is on the agent's monitor. Services set to manual start or disabled do not alert.

rules.name: SecurityGateway service down
rules.description: A watched service of the gateway does not answer, or greets to refuse service.

rules.name: SecurityGateway API not answering
rules.description: The REST API has stopped answering while the services still do. Only a monitor with an API key has the series.

rules.name: SecurityGateway delivery queue growing
rules.description: The delivery queue has grown by more than a hundred messages in two hours (delta(dumbmonit_securitygateway_counter{counter=~".*(delivery_queue\|queued_for_delivery).*"}[2h])): the mail server behind the gateway is probably refusing mail. The counter names come from the API as they are; if your version names the queue differently, adjust the matcher.

rules.description: No measurement received for more than three minutes. bottomk by (target) (1, time() - tlast_over_time(dumbmonit_up[7d]))

devices.label: Proxmox Mail Gateway
devices.summary: Mail queues and stuck mail, spam and virus traffic, quarantine, signature age.
devices.typical: Mail gateway filtering spam and viruses

credentials.label: Username / password (recommended)
credentials.help: Opens a two-hour session, renewed automatically. Proxmox Mail Gateway does not issue API tokens: this is its normal way in.

credentials.label: API token
credentials.help: Only if your gateway offers API tokens: Proxmox Mail Gateway 9 and earlier do not create any. Use the username and password instead.

setup.title: Create a read-only user in Proxmox Mail Gateway
steps:
Open Configuration → User Management → Users → Add, enter the user name below, a long password used nowhere else, and tick Enabled.
dumbmonit@pmg
Set its Role to Audit, then click Add.
In DumbMonit, enter the gateway address (for example mail.lan:8006), then this user name, realm included, and its password.
setup.warning: Proxmox Mail Gateway has no API tokens, so DumbMonit signs in with this password. It uses a self-signed certificate by default: tick "Accept an unverifiable certificate" in the options if the connection is refused.

rules.name: Mail queue growing
rules.description: The deferred mail queue has grown by more than a hundred messages in two hours (delta(dumbmonit_pmg_queue_messages{queue="deferred"}[2h])): the next hop is probably refusing mail. Growth rather than size, because a busy gateway always keeps a few dozen deferred.

rules.name: Mail stuck in the queue
rules.description: A message has been waiting in a queue for more than four hours. The age is a lower bound — qshape reports brackets — so the rule fires late rather than early. The notification names the queue.

rules.name: Mail gateway service stopped
rules.description: A service the gateway needs to accept and filter mail is stopped. A unit that is not installed has no series and cannot fire.

rules.name: Virus signatures out of date
rules.description: The ClamAV daily virus signatures are more than two days old: freshclam has stopped updating them and the gateway keeps filtering with last week's list.

rules.name: Spam rules out of date
rules.description: The SpamAssassin rules are more than eight days old. A channel that has never been updated has no date and no series.

rules.name: Quarantine filling up
rules.description: The spam quarantine has taken in more than a thousand messages in six hours (delta(dumbmonit_pmg_quarantine_messages{kind="spam"}[6h])): a campaign, or a rule that just put a legitimate domain in the bin.

rules.name: Mail gateway cluster degraded
rules.description: A gateway of the cluster is no longer in sync with the others: it filters with an out-of-date rule database. A standalone gateway has no series.

rules.name: Mail gateway certificate expiring
rules.description: A certificate of the mail gateway expires in less than fourteen days.

rules.name: Mail gateway updates pending
rules.description: More than twenty package updates are pending on the mail gateway.

devices.label: Mail server reputation
devices.summary: A mail domain's MX, or a mail server's public address, checked against the major DNS blocklists (Spamhaus, Barracuda, SpamCop…) or the ones you pick, with reverse DNS, SPF and DMARC, and the delisting page of every list that lists it. No API key needed.
examples: The public address of a mail server
devices.typical: Mail domain or server address against the DNS blocklists (Spamhaus, Barracuda, SpamCop…), reverse DNS, SPF, DMARC, delisting links

credentials.label: No key (recommended)
credentials.help: No key is needed. The blocklists are queried through this server's DNS resolver, or the one set under Resolver. Only Spamhaus can refuse, and only when that resolver is a public one (Google, Cloudflare, Quad9…): the monitor then says "Spamhaus refuses this resolver" and every other list keeps working.

credentials.label: Spamhaus DQS key (optional)
credentials.help: Only useful if Spamhaus refuses your resolver. A free Spamhaus Data Query Service key (low, non-commercial volumes) makes Spamhaus answer through any resolver, public ones included. It changes nothing for the other lists.

setup.title: Check a mail server against the blocklists
steps: Enter the domain you send mail for ("example.com"), or the public IP address the server sends from.
No API key is needed: leave the credential on No key.
Tick the blocklists to query under Blocklists, and add any other DNSBL zone under Custom lists.

If the monitor shows "Spamhaus refuses this resolver", set "Resolver" to your own recursive resolver, or choose the free Spamhaus DQS key as the credential.
https://www.spamhaus.com/data-access/free-data-query-service/
setup.warning: A blocklist that does not answer is shown as unknown, never as clean.

rules.name: Listed on a major blocklist
rules.description: An address or the domain is on Spamhaus (ZEN or DBL), Barracuda or SpamCop: a large share of its mail is refused.

rules.name: Listed on a blocklist
rules.description: An address or the domain is on a smaller list: Mailspike, UCEPROTECT, PSBL, SpamRATS, SURBL or URIBL.

rules.name: Mail server reverse DNS mismatch

setup.title: Monitor a PostgreSQL database
steps:
In psql, create a role that may only log in.
CREATE ROLE dumbmonit LOGIN PASSWORD 'a-long-password';

Allow it to connect from the DumbMonit host with this line in pg_hba.conf (adjust the address), then reload PostgreSQL.
host all dumbmonit 10.0.0.5/32 scram-sha-256
In DumbMonit, enter the server, for example db.home.lan:5433 (port 5432 by default), then the role's user and password.
Optional: replace the default query SELECT 1 with one that returns a single number, to chart it.

setup.title: Create a read-only Redis user
steps:
In redis-cli, create the user (Redis 6 or later, or Valkey).
ACL SETUSER dumbmonit on >a-long-password -@all +info +ping

Save it: ACL SAVE if the server uses an aclfile, CONFIG REWRITE otherwise.

In DumbMonit, enter the server address, for example cache.lan:6380, then the user and its password.

setup.title: Let DumbMonit read VictoriaMetrics' own health
steps:
Nothing to install: check from the DumbMonit host that VictoriaMetrics answers on its API port (8428 by default).
curl http://victoriametrics.lan:8428/health
If it runs with -httpAuth.username and -httpAuth.password, pick Username / password below; behind vmauth or a proxy that expects a bearer token, pick Bearer token.
In DumbMonit, enter the server address, for example "victoriametrics.lan" or "http://10.0.0.5:8428".

curl http://loki.lan:3100/ready
Loki has no login of its own: only if a reverse proxy in front asks for one, pick Username / password (or Bearer token) below.

setup.title: Create a read-only user and token in Graylog
steps:
Open System → Users and Teams → Create user, name it as follows, give it a long random password and assign the Reader role only.
dumbmonit
Open that user's Edit tokens page, create a token named after DumbMonit and copy it: Graylog shows it only once.

Optional, for Graylog's own notifications: with an account that can manage roles, create a role holding only notifications:read and give it to the dumbmonit user.
curl -u YOUR_USER -H 'X-Requested-By: cli' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X POST https://graylog.lan/api/roles -d '{"name":"DumbMonit Notifications","description":"Read system notifications","permissions":["notifications:read"],"read_only":false}'
curl -u YOUR_USER -H 'X-Requested-By: cli' -X PUT 'https://graylog.lan/api/roles/DumbMonit%20Notifications/members/dumbmonit'
In DumbMonit, enter the Graylog node address (for example graylog.lan, port 9000) and paste the token. In a cluster, add each node.
setup.warning: Do not reuse your own account: a leaked token carries every right of its user. Graylog serves plain HTTP unless TLS is configured: across an untrusted network, put it behind HTTPS.
